rows.evidence: P1's LKAI records on every invocation; the `none` arm (lkai_prof.handler + LKAI_PHASES=1) measures their cost against the REPORT-only `rep` arm
Init Duration, Restore Duration, Duration, Billed Duration, Max Memory Used on every row of invocations.jsonl; the `rep` arm is the zero-instrumentation control
lkai-p3-xray: TracingConfig Active on P1's zip, no code change; Lambda emits its own Initialization/Invocation/Overhead/Restore segments

lkai-p3-telemetry: extensions/lkai-telemetry (stdlib-only external extension, a layer) subscribed to platform events (platform.telemetrySubscription state Subscribed) and logged initStart / initRuntimeDone / initReport / restoreReport / runtimeDone spans / report

lkai-p3-cprofile: Python 3.12's cProfile runs on sys.monitoring, process-wide, so one profile sees the import thread, PR #77's load thread and the 32 download threads. Two concurrent profiles are refused ("Another profiling tool is already active", a first deploy failed init with Runtime.ExitError on exactly this). No native frames.

py-spy 0.4.2 static aarch64 binary shipped in the zip, run as the function's own child: `dump --nonblocking` of the parent works (process_vm_readv of the parent is allowed for a child), `record --nonblocking` records in lkai-p3-pyspy

`py-spy dump --native` and `dump` without --nonblocking of a child: "Failed to suspend process ... EPERM: Operation not permitted" (lambda-probe/q1.json -> py_spy.dump_child_native / dump_child_blocking). Suspending needs ptrace: PTRACE_SEIZE and PTRACE_ATTACH of our own child both EPERM. PR_SET_PTRACER is also EPERM.
rows.offline: works on the arm64 DevSpace, part 0xd40 (graviton/pyspy-native.txt) and costs about +29% per forward there (overhead_vs_plain.pyspy)

rows.evidence: perf_event_open of a user-space-only hardware cycles counter, software cpu-clock and software task-clock on the calling thread: all EPERM in every environment (lambda-probe -> syscalls.perf_event_open), with perf_event_paranoid 2, no PMU devices and CapEff 0. perf is also not in the runtime image.
rows.offline: works on the arm64 DevSpace, part 0xd40 (paranoid 2, armv8_pmuv3_0 PMU): perf stat, perf record -F 999 -g, graviton/perf-*

rows.evidence: bpf(BPF_MAP_CREATE, array) EPERM; unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1; /sys/fs/bpf, tracefs and debugfs absent; no CAP_BPF/CAP_SYS_ADMIN

rows.tool: ptrace-based tools (gdb, strace, ltrace, async stack dumpers)
rows.evidence: PTRACE_SEIZE and PTRACE_ATTACH on a child the probe started: EPERM; no gdb/strace/ltrace on PATH

setitimer(ITIMER_PROF) SIGPROF is delivered (19 signals in 0.2 s CPU, lambda-probe -> itimer_prof_sigprof). lkai-p3-sampler records the interrupted PC and LR of whichever thread is on CPU, tagged by phase, and symbolises in the function from /proc/self/maps and the ELF .symtab/.dynsym of the shipped libraries (the shipped ggml/llama libraries keep .symtab: libggml-cpu-armv8.6_1.so, the variant part 0xd40 loads, has 2,459 FUNC symbols, 733 of them KleidiAI kai_*). Limits: no stack walk (PC + caller only); one SIGPROF pending per process, so the effective rate per CPU-second is below 1 kHz (reported as effective_hz_per_cpu_s); CPU time only, so waits (S3 reads, futexes) are invisible.
The runtime is python3.12; there is no JVM. Its Python counterparts are py-spy and cProfile above.
